claims.claim: The paper asks how to conceptualize AI system architecture around human decision needs.
claims.qualification: Motivational question, not a test of a system.

claims.claim: Fast and slow thinking are extended with a proposed control role.
claims.qualification: Architectural proposal; no independent neurological System 3 is established. Figure 1 uses nondirectional connectors without arrowheads and does not specify a runtime execution sequence.

claims.claim: Interfaces, bias, imbalance and control allocation motivate the third role.
claims.qualification: Motivation does not prove bias elimination, stability or optimal switching.

claims.claim: A decision catalog can capture 16 requirements elements including automation level.
claims.qualification: No evaluation of checklist completeness or effectiveness.

claims.claim: The paper classifies intuitive, rational and control AI roles.
claims.qualification: Examples are broad; only some aspects of LLM use are characterized as intuitive.

claims.claim: Application architecture includes actor, interface, application, agent and environment.
claims.qualification: Principal-agent delegation is a conceptual lens; not proof of agent alignment.

claims.claim: Data architecture includes actor, interface, data system and data.
claims.qualification: No comparison of data platforms or empirical data-bias treatment.

claims.claim: Algorithm architecture includes algorithm, input, output and model/product.
claims.qualification: Training/validation/test/production are generic categories, not an evaluation dataset.

claims.claim: Four automation levels include two semi-automated variants. Manual uses human Systems 1-3; semi-automated replaces either System 1 or System 2 with AI while System 3 remains human; automated uses AI Systems 1-2 and human System 3 with full human control; autonomous uses AI Systems 1-3 without human intervention or control. Humans remain accountable at all levels.
claims.qualification: Original source Table VI extends off-page; parent reviewer recovered and visually checked drawing content using a widened in-memory page canvas without altering the PDF. Pattern mapping is now resolved. Proposed allocation is not a safety certification or proof of effective intervention.

claims.claim: The source discusses social, economic, understanding and enterprise-architecture implications.
claims.qualification: No measured social, economic, safety or communication outcomes.

claims.claim: The adaptive EA extension adds decision and algorithm architecture domains.
claims.qualification: Proposed integration; Figure 4 arrows highlight additions rather than flows. Prose has a Figure 4/5 cross-reference inconsistency.

claims.claim: The text names initiate, discover, implement, govern and adapt as five iterative stages. Figure 5 places Initiate, Discover and Implement in three panels with a double-headed Govern & Adapt arrow spanning them.
claims.qualification: Govern and Adapt are not downstream-only sequential boxes. No deployment or optimized project-management protocol is evaluated.

claims.claim: The economic discussion cites an external claim of more than 80% AI project failure.
claims.qualification: Not measured by Gill; denominator and causal interpretation not independently verified here.

claims.claim: Switching conditions, freedom, control allocation, observability, traceability and interfaces remain open research questions.
claims.qualification: Do not present these as implementation details already solved.
